sium, magnesium, and phosphorus may also occur as a result 
of intracellular shifts associated with carbohydrate delivery and
anabolism. In addition, serum phosphorus may be decreased
secondary to severe respiratory alkalosis as a result of increased 
clearance across the dialysis membrane with continuous renal
replacement therapy (CRRT) or because of intracellular shifts. 
Hypophosphatemia also occurs in the refeeding syndrome, 
malnutrition, and diuretic therapy. Serum levels of potassium, 
magnesium, and phosphorus should therefore be monitored
frequently to assess the need for additional supplementation. 
Delivery of potassium, magnesium, and phosphorus should be 
individualized according to serum levels.67
